newsitem.title: JORDAN: Israel to pump water to Jordan on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Israel to pump water to Jordan on Tuesday.

text.p: Jordan will open the tap on Tuesday to channel millions of cubic metres of water from Israel to its parched reservoirs, fulfilling a long-delayed Israeli pledge under a 1994 peace accord, Jordanian officials said on Monday.
The fresh water supply, agreed at a meeting of experts last week, is aimed at resolving a crisis between the two countries over supply of water to Jordan which blew up earlier this month.

Officials declined to say how much water Jordan would be receiving and water ministry officials were not available for comment. Newspaper reports have said it could be up to 30 million cubic metres a year.

Israeli water ministry sources said on Friday Israel would supply Jordan with fresh water, either from the Sea of Galilee or from underground sources, until a plan for desalination of 50 million cubic metres of Israeli water a year in Jordan could be implemented.

The water is part of a package of water supplies Israel pledged to supply Jordan with under a 1994 peace treaty. The two countries disagreed on how to implement the accord and Jordan accused Israel of reneging on the deal.

The dispute reached a crisis in early May when Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan cancelled a meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The interim agreement follows a secret meeting between King Hussein and Netanyahu at the Red Sea port of Aqaba.
